links.outcome: LRM recommendation quality versus human MDT decisions and versus each other, graded by oncologists
links.effect: GPT-5-Thinking avg_rec exceeded MDT grade in both phases (retrograde 4.90 vs 4.14, P<.001; anterograde 4.79 vs 4.34, P<.001); Deepseek-v3-r1 exceeded MDT only in retrograde phase (4.56 vs 4.14, P<.001; anterograde P=.15).
links.quote: The mean (95% CI) GPT-5-Thinking avg_rec exceeded MDT grade in both phases (retrograde: 4.90, 4.84-4.95 vs 4.14, 3.96-4.33; P<.001; anterograde: 4.79, 4.69-4.89 vs 4.34, 4.16-4.52; P<.001); Deepseek-v3-r1 exceeded MDT in the retrograde phase (4.56, 4.40-4.72 vs 4.14, 3.96-4.33; P<.001) but not the anterograde phase (4.54, 4.41-4.67 vs 4.34, 4.16-4.52; P=.15).

unlisted_practices: Comparing LLM recommendations with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions using blinded expert Likert grading
Testing whether clinician awareness of AI benchmarking (Hawthorne-type effect) changes team decision quality

screen.reason: The study evaluates LLM reasoning models on retrospective and prospective lung cancer MDT cases compared with human MDT decisions, measuring diagnostic/therapeutic recommendation accuracy/quality rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
